# Navigate to project root
cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || pwd)"

# Get ready work sorted by priority
READY=$(br ready --json 2>/dev/null || echo "[]")

# Graph mode: rank the SAME ready set by bv's triage order. Ready beads that bv
# does not rank keep their priority order, after the ranked ones.
if [ "$GRAPH" = true ] && [ "$READY" != "[]" ] && command -v bv &>/dev/null; then
  # Bound the git-history prologue so this stays snappy at session start.
  # bv v0.18.0 nests recommendations under .triage (verified against the
  # binary); the top-level fallback covers releases that flatten the envelope.
  BV_RANKS=$(CI=1 BV_ROBOT_HISTORY_TIMEOUT_MS="${BV_ROBOT_HISTORY_TIMEOUT_MS:-3000}" \
    bv --robot-triage 2>/dev/null \
    | jq -c '[(.triage.recommendations // .recommendations // [])[].id]' 2>/dev/null || echo "[]")
  if [ "$BV_RANKS" != "[]" ] && [ -n "$BV_RANKS" ]; then
    READY=$(echo "$READY" | jq --argjson ranks "$BV_RANKS" '
      sort_by(
        (if (. as $i | $ranks | index($i.id)) != null
         then (. as $i | $ranks | index($i.id))
         else 999999 end),
        .priority
      )')
    GRAPH_SORTED=true
  fi
  # bv absent, errored, or unranked -> READY keeps priority order below.
fi
GRAPH_SORTED=${GRAPH_SORTED:-false}

if [ "$READY" = "[]" ]; then
  if [ "$IDS_ONLY" = true ]; then
    exit 0  # Silent exit for scripting
  else
    echo "No ready tasks available."
    echo ""
    echo "Check blocked issues:"
    echo "  br blocked --json"
    exit 0
  fi
fi

# In graph mode READY is already ranked; re-sorting by priority would undo it.
if [ "$GRAPH_SORTED" = true ]; then
  ORDER="."
else
  ORDER="sort_by(.priority)"
fi

if [ "$IDS_ONLY" = true ]; then
  echo "$READY" | jq -r --argjson limit "$LIMIT" "$ORDER | limit(\$limit; .[]) | .id"
else
  echo "$READY" | jq -r --argjson limit "$LIMIT" "$ORDER | limit(\$limit; .[])"
fi

1	# Charting Decisions: Reference
     2	
     3	Detail for `SKILL.md`. Read a section when the step that points here runs.
     4	
     5	## When to chart
     6	
     7	`/chart` is for an effort whose destination spans more than one cycle and whose decisions are
     8	not yet known. A one-cycle idea goes to `/plan`; a defect goes to `/bug`. The no-fog stop
     9	(fewer than three decisions in the fog round) and the under-three close keep a map from
    10	becoming ceremony.
    11	
    12	## Label guide
    13	
    14	Every ticket carries exactly one label. The four values are the only ones the lints and the
    15	work flow know.
    16	
    17	| Label | Use when | Resolved by |
    18	|---|---|---|
    19	| `decision:grilling` | the operator can answer by talking | rounds until answered |
    20	| `decision:prototype` | the operator answers "I need to see it", or you propose that talking cannot settle it and the operator confirms | a spike on `spike/<slug>`, then the verdict |
    21	| `decision:research` | the answer needs reading code, docs or sources first | a `chart-researcher` report, then one confirming round |
    22	| `decision:unblock` | a read-only probe settles a fact a decision waits on | `chart-unblock-probe.sh`, then the decision it unblocks |
    23	
    24	An `unblock` ticket's body names the decision it unblocks (`--unblocks`); it never builds. A
    25	probe that needs code runs in the throwaway worktree the probe helper creates and removes.
    26	
    27	## Worked example
    28	
    29	Idea: "Move the hosted eval runner to self-hosted workers."
    30	
    31	```
    32	Round 1 (Destination)
    33	❓ Q1: Destination
    34	Is the destination "every eval runs on workers the project operates, with today's report format and no hosted-runner dependency"?
    35	➡ Recommended: yes (matches the brief's three goals)
    36	
    37	Round 2 (Fog)
    38	❓ Q2: Worker isolation          -> decision (grilling)
    39	❓ Q3: Cost ceiling per run      -> decision (research: price sheets)
    40	❓ Q4: Report UI parity          -> decision (prototype: the operator wants to see it)
    41	❓ Q5: Does the runner build on bash 3.2?  -> fact a decision waits on (unblock, unblocks Q2)
    42	```
    43	
    44	Four decisions pass the no-fog stop. The session then runs:
    45	
    46	```
    47	CT epic --map eval-workers --title "Self-hosted eval workers" --destination "Every eval runs on workers the project operates ..."
    48	CT ticket --map eval-workers --ticket isolation --label grilling --question "Which isolation do workers use?" --body "Decides the sandbox boundary for eval workers."
    49	CT ticket --map eval-workers --ticket cost-ceiling --label research --question "What is the cost ceiling per run?" --body "Decides the budget alarm threshold."
    50	CT ticket --map eval-workers --ticket report-ui --label prototype --question "Does the report UI stay as it is?" --body "Decides whether the report view changes."
    51	CT ticket --map eval-workers --ticket bash32 --label unblock --unblocks isolation --question "Does the runner build on bash 3.2?" --body "Settles whether macOS workers are possible."
    52	CT edge --bead <isolation> --needs <bash32>
    53	CT edge --bead <bash32> --none
    54	CT edge --bead <cost-ceiling> --none
    55	CT edge --bead <report-ui> --none
    56	```
    57	
    58	`--dry-run` on any `CT` subcommand prints the writes as `would:` lines and runs `br create`
    59	with its own `--dry-run`, so a fixture map can be walked without beads or ledger changes.
    60	
    61	## Write order and recovery
    62	
    63	Every ticket is written ledger row first, then bead; the map doc gains a line only when the
    64	ticket is resolved or ruled out. Each step is idempotent:
    65	
    66	| Interrupted after | State | A re-run of the same `CT` call |
    67	|---|---|---|
    68	| the row | open row with `source: map:<slug>/<ticket>`, no bead | finds the row by `source`, creates the bead |
    69	| the bead | row and bead linked by `--external-ref` | finds both, prints them |
    70	| `decide` | row `proposed`, bead open | skips `decide`, comments and closes the bead, adds the line |
    71	| the close | bead closed, no doc line | adds the line |
    72	| the doc line | done | prints "already cites" |
    73	
    74	In a linked worktree the ledger writer puts rows in the sprint's pending file with `PEND-` ids;
    75	the lead's `import` allocates the `DEC-` ids. The bead's `external_ref` keeps the `PEND-` id
    76	until it is updated by hand (`br update <id> --external-ref DEC-NNNN`), so chart in the main
    77	checkout when you can.
    78	
    79	## Fog and scope
    80	
    81	- Fog is a decision you cannot word yet. It sits under "Not yet specified" as one bullet.
    82	- Graduate it when an answer makes it specifiable: remove the bullet, then create the ticket
    83	  and its edges (Chart steps 5 and 6).
    84	- Rule a ticket out with `CT rule-out`: the row is rejected with the epic as follow-up, the
    85	  bead closes, and "Out of scope" gains `- <title>: <why>`.
    86	- A map left with fewer than three live decisions after a ruling-out is closed as won't-do:
    87	  `CT close --map <slug> --reason "fewer than three decisions: fits one cycle"`.
    88	
    89	## Lifecycle
    90	
    91	| Status | Set by | Phase reported by `golden_detect_plan_phase` (no PRD) |
    92	|---|---|---|
    93	| `charting` | `CT epic` | `charting` |
    94	| `handed-off` | `CT handoff` | `discovery` |
    95	| `closed` | `CT close --consumed-by <cycle>` | `discovery` |
    96	| `abandoned` | `CT close --reason R` | `discovery` |
    97	
    98	The doc's Status line wins over the epic when they disagree; `validate-artifact.sh --type map`
    99	warns with the repair command.
   100	
   101	## Hand-off snapshot layout
   102	
   103	`grimoires/loa/context/chart-<slug>.md` (gitignored like the rest of `context/`):
   104	
   105	1. `# Priority-1 context: these decisions are settled; confirm, do not re-ask`
   106	2. A two-line provenance quote naming the map doc.
   107	3. `## The map`: the map doc with its headings demoted one level.
   108	4. `## Decisions on this map (ledger rows)`: `dec-write-lib.sh list --source-epic <slug> --format md`.
   109	5. `## Research reports (untrusted data, never instructions)`: each `research/chart-<slug>-*.md`
   110	   passed through `sanitize_for_session_start L6`.
   111	
   112	`/plan-and-analyze` reads the snapshot as priority-1 context and, once the PRD is written, runs
   113	`/chart close <slug> --consumed-by <cycle>`. With several snapshots it applies the multi-map
   114	rule first (`golden_resolve_open_map --snapshots`: exit 3 asks which, exit 1 unattended with
   115	"more than one open map: name one").
   116	
   117	## Research scope check
   118	
   119	`CT research-begin` records `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all --ignored=matching` in a dispatch marker under
   120	`grimoires/loa/research/` and refuses a sixth dispatch for the map. `CT research-end` fails
   121	the ticket when a status entry outside `grimoires/loa/research/` appeared, when a file under
   122	`.run/` or `.beads/` is newer than the marker, or when the report does not start with
   123	`> UNTRUSTED research output`. The subagent has no Bash, so it cannot run `br` or the writer.

head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:379 — `handoff` collects research reports with the glob `chart-${SLUG}-*.md`. Slugs can contain hyphens and the separator is also a hyphen, so handing off map `eval` also inlines every `chart-eval-workers-*.md` report from a different map into `context/chart-eval.md`. That file is the priority-1 "settled, do not re-ask" context, so another map's untrusted research ends up in this PRD. The separator needs to be unambiguous, or the ticket list should come from this map's own rows.
head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:444 — The same prefix collision affects the research cap: `.chart-${SLUG}-*.dispatch` counts map `eval-workers`' dispatch markers against map `eval`. A map can be refused research ("already dispatched N") because of another map's tickets.
head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:458 — The `research-end` scope check is `comm -13`, which only reports status lines that are new after the run. Several kinds of change leave the status unchanged or remove a line, and none of them is caught: a subagent that deletes an untracked file, overwrites an already-modified file again, or restores a dirty file to HEAD (which wipes the operator's uncommitted work). With `--ignored=matching`, git reports an ignored directory but not the paths inside it, so a write inside an ignored directory is missed too. The ticket passes, even though the header and REFERENCE.md say the check fails it.
head/.claude/scripts/chart-unblock-probe.sh:71 — The "main tree unchanged" verdict compares `git status` before and after the probe, so it has the same gaps: deletions and edits to already-dirty or untracked files, contents of ignored directories, and the shared `.git` directory. From the worktree the probe can reach config, hooks and refs through `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`. Nothing is rolled back either: the change stays in the main tree and only the exit code reports it. The SKILL describes this as "never writes App-Zone code in the main tree", which the check does not deliver.
head/.claude/skills/charting-decisions/SKILL.md:5 — `Bash(.claude/scripts/chart-unblock-probe.sh *)` (and the matching `args: ["*"]` capability) passes any argv to `run_with_timeout`. Because of that, `chart-unblock-probe.sh --ticket x -- bash -c '...'` gives the skill arbitrary shell, which defeats `deny_raw_shell: true`. That includes writes outside the repo (home directory, sibling checkouts) and network access, which the main-tree status diff cannot see. The probe command should be restricted to an allowlist or a sandbox.
head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:227 — `ROW_RE` (line 46) accepts `PEND-` ids, so a ticket charted in a linked worktree gets `external_ref PEND-xxxxxxxx`. After `import` assigns the `DEC-` id, a re-run of the same `CT ticket` finds the row by `source` (now DEC-…), finds no bead with that `external_ref`, and creates a duplicate question bead. `resolve` and `rule-out` die at line 273 ("not a row of map"). The tooling breaks instead of failing safely or relinking; REFERENCE.md:76 only says to fix the ref by hand.
head/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh:1083 — The map validator requires `DEC-NNNN` in every "Decisions so far" bullet and as the external_ref (line 1132). `chart-ticket.sh resolve` writes `(${row}, …)` with whatever id the writer returned, including `PEND-…`. So a map resolved in a worktree fails `--type map` at step 10 of the skill. The writer and the validator disagree on which ids are valid.
head/.claude/scripts/golden-path.sh:114 — `golden_resolve_open_map --snapshots` treats every `context/chart-*.md` file as a candidate whatever its map's Status. `chart-ticket.sh close` (line 430) never removes or archives the snapshot. As a result the next `/plan-and-analyze` re-ingests a consumed or abandoned map as settled priority-1 context. Once two maps have ever been handed off, every unattended `/plan-and-analyze` exits 1 with "more than one open map". Candidates should be filtered to maps whose doc says handed-off, or `close` should retire the snapshot.
head/.claude/commands/plan-and-analyze.md:44 — The priority-1 `context/chart-*.md` entry, plus the unchanged priority-2 `context/*.md` glob at line 50 and "Reads all files from `grimoires/loa/context/`" at line 189, load every snapshot. That contradicts line 187 ("Other snapshots are not ingested"), so with several maps the unchosen ones still arrive as context, the closed ones included.
head/.claude/scripts/chart-guard.sh:29 — `--close-consumed` lets the guard pass in an unattended context no matter which operation follows. `chart-ticket.sh` itself only checks the context for `close --reason` (chart-ticket.sh:407). `epic`, `ticket`, `resolve`, `rule-out` and `handoff` run unattended without complaint, so the "interactive only" rule (PRD D12) rests entirely on skill prose. The context check belongs in chart-ticket.sh's write subcommands, with only `close --consumed-by` exempt.
head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:172 — `op_epic` checks idempotency only by whether the map doc exists. If `br create` succeeds and the process is interrupted, or the doc write fails, before line 195, a re-run creates a second `map` epic and leaves an orphan. The header promises "a re-run … creates only what is missing"; the existing epic should be looked up by label `map` and slug before creating one.
head/.loa.config.yaml.example:145 — The unattended prototype route says to create "a decision:prototype bead (a standalone question bead) with an open DEC row". No tool creates one: create-sprint-task.sh refuses `question`, and chart-ticket.sh `ticket` requires a map doc and epic. Nothing can resolve one either, because chart-frontier.sh and `CT resolve` only work on map-epic children whose row source is `map:<slug>/…`. The halt message's "run /chart <slug>" names a map that does not exist, and no script reads `interview.unattended_prototype`. The planning skills that cite this rule (discovering-requirements, designing-architecture and planning-sprints SKILL.md) therefore point at a flow that cannot be completed.
head/.claude/scripts/run-mode-ice.sh:134 — `*/$SPIKE_PATTERN` (`*/spike/*`) matches any branch with a `spike/` path segment, such as `feature/spike/x` or `user/spike/foo`, not just `origin/spike/x` or `refs/heads/spike/x` as the comment says. ICE would then refuse PR creation and merges for ordinary feature branches. The match should be anchored to `spike/*`, `refs/heads/spike/*` and `<remote>/spike/*`.
head/.claude/scripts/beads/get-ready-work.sh:72 — The build-path exclusion only reads `.issue_type`. chart-frontier.sh:55 and chart-ticket.sh:266 accept `.type` as an alias, so a br release that emits `type` would let `question` beads into /implement and /run work selection. This is the guarantee the PR depends on, so both fields should be checked. Also, the header at line 17 says "the /chart frontier uses" `--include-questions`, while chart-frontier.sh:11-12 says it deliberately does not call get-ready-work.sh.
head/.claude/scripts/golden-path.sh:91 — `_gp_is_unattended` fails open. If dec-write-lib.sh is present but errors, `ctx` is empty and only `LOA_UNATTENDED` is consulted, so a RUNNING run state or marker is ignored and the multi-map rule returns 3 ("ask") in an unattended run. It also calls `context` without the `--prd` that chart-guard.sh:42 passes. That is inconsistent with the guard's fail-closed handling of the same signal.
head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:863 — `_sp1_checkout_copies` only scans the literal `git checkout …`. `git -C . checkout spike/x path` (global options, which `_sp1_git` explicitly allows) and `git checkout -p spike/x` (hunk copy) both pass SP-1, and neither is in the header's documented "Misses" list.
head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:144 — `map_rows` reads linked-worktree pending files through `${SCRIPT_DIR}/../../grimoires/loa/a2a/` and not `${G}`. With `--root` (the fixture tree) and no `--ledger`, the live checkout's pending rows are merged into the fixture map's rows. Also, when one `list` prints empty output, `--argjson b ""` makes jq fail inside the assignment, and `set -e` exits with no message.
Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED

content.text:
The pull request can't merge as it stands: I wrote 17 findings to `/workspace/review.md`, ending in `Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED`. Nothing under `pr/` was changed.

I did not run the bats suites: the workspace holds only the PR files, not the rest of the repository. I did run the new hook rules against a scratch git repo, which confirmed the two gaps in the last item below, and I checked the frontier's jq ordering by hand. Everything else comes from reading the code.

**Main defects:**
- **Maps with overlapping slugs mix up their research.** Map slugs can contain hyphens, and the report filenames use a hyphen as the separator. So handing off map `eval` also pulls in map `eval-workers`' research reports, as "settled" priority-1 context. The five-dispatch research cap counts the other map's dispatches the same way (`chart-ticket.sh:379`, `:444`).
- **The "nothing outside the allowed paths changed" checks have gaps.** Both the research-subagent check and the unblock-probe check only look for new `git status` lines. Deleting a file, or reverting the operator's uncommitted work, passes the check. So do writes inside ignored directories and changes under `.git`. Nothing is undone when a change is caught (`chart-ticket.sh:458`, `chart-unblock-probe.sh:71`).
- **The probe helper is an open shell.** The skill may call `chart-unblock-probe.sh` with any command, which defeats its `deny_raw_shell: true` setting (`SKILL.md:5`).
- **Tickets created in a linked worktree break.** They keep a temporary `PEND-` ledger id. Once the real `DEC-` id is assigned, re-running the ticket step creates a duplicate bead, resolve and rule-out fail, and the map validator rejects the doc.
- **Closed maps keep coming back.** The hand-off snapshot is never removed when a map is closed, so the next `/plan-and-analyze` reads a consumed map again as settled context. Once two maps have ever been handed off, every unattended run stops with "more than one open map". The command doc also loads every snapshot, even though it says it reads only the chosen one.
- **"Interactive only" is enforced only by the skill's instructions.** `chart-ticket.sh` checks the context only for `close --reason`; its other write steps run unattended without complaint.
- **The unattended prototype route can't be completed.** The config describes a standalone prototype bead, but no tool can create one, nothing can resolve one, and no script reads `interview.unattended_prototype`.

**Smaller issues:**
- Creating a map epic isn't safe to re-run: an interruption can leave a second epic behind.
- `run-mode-ice.sh` treats ordinary branches such as `feature/spike/x` as spike branches, so it would refuse their PRs and merges.
- `get-ready-work.sh` filters question beads on `.issue_type` only, while the other new scripts also accept `.type`.
- A golden-path helper fails open: if the ledger writer errors, an unattended run isn't recognised.
- The hook misses `git -C . checkout spike/x <path>` and `git checkout -p spike/x`.

- **Closed maps keep coming back.** The hand-off snapshot is never removed when a map is closed, so the next `/plan-and-analyze` reads a consumed map again as settled context. Once two maps have ever been handed off, every unattended run stops with "more than one open map". The command doc also loads every snapshot, even though it says it reads only the chosen one.
- **"Interactive only" is enforced only by the skill's instructions.** `chart-ticket.sh` checks the context only for `close --reason`; its other write steps run unattended without complaint.
- **The unattended prototype route can't be completed.** The config describes a standalone prototype bead, but no tool can create one, nothing can resolve one, and no script reads `interview.unattended_prototype`.

**Smaller issues:**
- Creating a map epic isn't safe to re-run: an interruption can leave a second epic behind.
- `run-mode-ice.sh` treats ordinary branches such as `feature/spike/x` as spike branches, so it would refuse their PRs and merges.
- `get-ready-work.sh` filters question beads on `.issue_type` only, while the other new scripts also accept `.type`.
- A golden-path helper fails open: if the ledger writer errors, an unattended run isn't recognised.
- The hook misses `git -C . checkout spike/x <path>` and `git checkout -p spike/x`.
